questions.question:

Customers WHERE (TRUE OR !TRUE) AND NOT(!FALSE) OR TRUE?

Given the table mytable, where field1 is either 1 or 0 and field2 is either 1 or 0, what will
be the result of the query “SELECT field1^field2 FROM mytable”?
options: A 0 for each row where field1 and field2 are 0; all other rows will be 1
Only rows from mytable where either field1 or field2 is 1

questions.question:
The sales table above was originally created in error with the following create statement.
What statement had to be run before the data was inserted?
CREATE TABLE `sales` (
`mem_no` INT NOT NULL,
`month` VARCHAR(45) NULL,
`gross` DOUBLE NULL,
`net` DOUBLE NULL,
PRIMARY KEY (`mem_no`));
options: ALTER TABLE sales MODIFY mem_no ALLOW DUPS
ALTER TABLE sales MODIFY COLUMN mem_no INT NULL
ALTER TABLE sales DROP PRIMARY INDEX

ALTER TABLE sales MODIFY INDEX ("cust_ no") REMOVE PRIMARY
CONSTRAINT

questions.question: The highest normalization form the customer table meets is _______.

How many rows would the following query produce?
SELECT name
FROM member_info a
INNER JOIN sales b ON a.mem_no = b.mem_no
WHERE a.mem_no IN
(SELECT mem_no
FROM sales
GROUP BY mem_no
HAVING SUM(gross) > 1500)

Why will this query result in a syntax error?
SELECT name
FROM member_info
WHERE mem_no NOT IN
(SELECT mem_no
FROM sales
GROUP BY month
WHERE AVG(net) > 500)
options: Cannot use an aggregate function in a WHERE clause
Cannot have two WHERE clauses in the same query
NOT is not allowed in this context
GROUP BY column is not part of the field list
